memoryTip: Mis + construe (build meaning) — you build the wrong meaning from what was said.
correctPassage: Readers should not misconstrue correlation as proof of causation.
wrongPassages: She carefully misconstrued the blueprint so every joint lined up perfectly.
They hired an editor to misconstrue the draft into clear, precise prose.
The translator misconstrued every line so faithfully that nothing was changed.

memoryTip: De-nigrate: blacken someone’s name — smear them with unfair criticism.
correctPassage: It is unfair to denigrate the entire field for one flawed study.
wrongPassages: The coach denigrated the team by praising each player after the win.
Reviewers denigrated the novel with a glowing front-page recommendation.
She denigrated the lab by funding its next three research proposals.

memoryTip: Make null — cancel it so it no longer counts or has force.
correctPassage: A clerical error threatened to nullify the results of the election.
wrongPassages: The court will nullify the contract by signing both parties into a longer deal.
She will nullify the schedule by confirming every meeting for the week ahead.
They nullify the gap by adding data that strengthened the original finding.

definition: irrelevant or unrelated to the matter at hand
memoryTip: Extra stuff that doesn’t belong — noise outside the real point.
correctPassage: Cut extraneous detail that does not advance the argument.
wrongPassages: The thesis sentence was extraneous: every later paragraph depended on it.
Judges called the key evidence extraneous because it decided the case.
Her extraneous outline listed only the steps the team actually needed.

definition: collect or form into a mass or cluster
memoryTip: Ag-glomerate like glue — bits clump into one sticky mass.
correctPassage: Dust particles agglomerate into larger clusters in humid air.
wrongPassages: The chemist will agglomerate the solution until every crystal fully dissolves.
They agglomerated the crowd by opening three extra exits and clearing the hall.
She agglomerated the report by cutting it from forty pages down to two.
